messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p95 latency > 1200ms on /v1/generate (us-west-2 canary cohort). Thresholds breached x3 in 2m. dc: us-west-2; cohort: canary-wave-7. Link: https://metrics/reports/1865432199\ndeploy-bot: Deploy r2026.02 -> canary-wave-7 completed 30s ago (sha: ab12cd).
alice (oncall): ack, I'm on it. paging eng-runtime @ben
ben (eng-runtime): looking now. I can see sustained kernel fallback events on canary hosts, batch window shrinking to 16ms -> throughput drop ~28%. grabbing logs...
ben (eng-runtime): log snippet: ```2026-03-10T12:16:20Z kernel_select: fallback->scalar_quantized path chosen; prefetch_retries=12; batch_window_ms=16```
jamie (sre-lead): what is customer impact? severity?
support-liaison: CS: 3 high-touch customers reporting timeouts and elevated token latency, ~5% API error increase. Tickets opened PROD-4421/4422/4423.
alice (oncall): quick mitigation: toggled feature-flag batch-adaptive=off for canary-wave-7. no significant improvement on p95, throughput slight bump. preparing rollback.
deploy-bot: Rollback r2026.02 -> previous r2026.01 initiated for canary-wave-7. Rolling across 8 hosts. progress: 2/8 -> 5/8 -> 8/8
ben (eng-runtime): after rollback, p50/p95 trending back toward baseline but we still see intermittent batch fragmentation. root cause hypothesis: kernel selector change in r2026.02 prefers quantized path for short sequences; that path triggers aggressive prefetch which thrashes GPU memory and collapses batching under certain traffic shapes.
kira (pm): timeline for full rollback to control plane? any customer-facing note we should prepare now?
support-liaison: recommend short note: "we experienced degraded latency for a subset of requests during a canary release; mitigation applied and full rollback completed; no data exposure." will draft.
ajamie (sre-lead): assigning Sev2 for tracking. create incident ticket I-2026-0310 and link postmortem.
alice (oncall): handoff notes for night oncall: rollback completed at 12:24 UTC, canary hosts stable, p95 back within 10% of baseline. Actions remaining: (1) block the kernel-selector change from auto-rollout, (2) force legacy kernel affinity on affected fleets, (3) run synthetic soak for 2 hours, (4) postmortem + evals on workload distribution.
ben (eng-runtime): quick commands I ran: ```kubectl exec -it pod/canary-3 -- curl -X POST /admin/force_kernel?affinity=legacy``` That reduced prefetch retries immediately.
kira (pm): noted. I'll coordinate customer comms and update status page once we have final numbers.
jamie (sre-lead): leaving this in alice's hands until 14:00 UTC then hand to night oncall @tom. please attach perf diffs and kernel selector patch link in the incident ticket.
alice (oncall): handing off to night oncall. logs, perf graphs, and rollback artifacts uploaded to I-2026-0310. ping me for any questions.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation applied (rollback + feature-flag) — system metrics stable for 10m. Monitoring will continue.
support-liaison: comms draft posted in #incidents-drafts. will send to affected accounts after final validation.
ben (eng-runtime): short-term patch: disable auto-select quantized-kernel for seq_len < 128 and add backpressure on prefetch. long-term: revisit kernel selection heuristics + add unit tests for traffic shapes.
alice (oncall): last note: severity Sev2, customer impact contained, next steps in incident ticket. handing off now.
